rows: Hurricane-like conditions reported about one mile southeast of Dreyfoos which lasted for nearly thirty minutes. Some of the damage reported included a door blown off a hayshed...a feed bunker damaged...and several windows blown out of a home.

An EF-0 tornado was video documented northeast of Briscoe. No damage was reported.
Golf ball size hail was reported 5 miles northwest of Allison.
Quarter size hail was reported 8 miles north-northwest of Allison.
A storm chaser measured 3 1/3 inch diameter hailstones 2 miles northeast of Allison.
Quarter size hail was reported 10 miles northwest of Canadian.

Trained spotters reported golf ball size hail 5 miles west-southwest of Glazier. The hail started as quarter size and then became larger.
Half dollar size hail was reported 6 miles northwest of Canadian.

This tornado was reported by multiple storm chasers and also touched down within the damage path of the first EF-2 tornado. Eyewitness reports indicate that this tornado stayed over open fields and cause no additional damage.

Winds up to 70 mph blew down trees which blocked Highway 83 2 miles north-northwest of Canadian.
The automated weather observing station at the Canadian airport measured a wind gust of 60 mph.
The West Texas Mesonet site located 6 miles east of Canadian measured a wind gust of 77 mph.
This tornado began in Roberts County. The path details of this tornado are based on trained spotter accounts and radar information. No damage was observed. A rating of EF-0 was assigned.

Much of the track of this storm was across farmland which was inaccessible. Therefore, track width and tornado strengths are based on locations where it crossed roadways. One home sustained roof damage. Additional damage included trees, fences, metal sheds, and oil field equipmen…
Quarter size hail fell 6 miles north of Canadian.

A brief tornado crossed Highway 60 about 3 miles south of Canadian. Minimal tree damage was found, consistent with EF-0 damage and estimated peak winds of 74 mph. A storm spotter witnessed this tornado.
Trees were reported down in Canadian.

A narrow tornado track of tree damage was found by the survey team. The tornado was reported by several chasers and spotters. Tree damage was consistent with EF-0 damage and estimated peak wind of 75 mph.
The West Texas Mesonet site located 6 miles east of Canadian measured a 74 mph wind gust.
Multiple tree limbs about 6 inches in diameter were reported down along Highway 83, 6 miles north-northwest of Gageby.

A tornado was witnessed by the Roger Mills County, Oklahoma Fire Department on the Texas side of the state line. The tornado then moved into Oklahoma shortly after developing. Some damage was reported to a wheat field. The tornado was assigned an EF-0 rating.
A brief rope tornado was witnessed by a storm spotter approximately 5 miles south-southwest of Higgins. An EF-U rating was assigned as the tornado remained in open grassland.
Tennis ball sized hail reported at 555 PM.
Quarter sized hail reported east of Canadian.
Thunderstorm wind gust up to 60 MPH.
Large tree branches down due to winds from thunderstorm.
Thunderstorm wind gust measured up to 62 MPH with storm.
A tornado touched down in rural Hemphill County northwest of Glazier. The tornado caused damage to trees, power poles and out building equivalent to a lower end EF1.
Late report of nickel to quarter sized hail.
Mostly pea to quarter size. Found one stone that was the size of a ping pong ball.
Mostly nickel size hail with a few quarters at the Canadian Golf Course.
Broadcast media relayed pictures of damage to skylight and windshield and also pictures of the hail.
Storm chaser reported quarter size hail via spotter network.
Canadian West Texas Mesonet reported wind gust.

Other reports of 60 MPH gusts in the area.
Quarter size hail lasted about 3 minutes just northwest of Glazier on Highway 60. Wind was estimated 40 to 50 mph with a few peak gusts around 60 mph.
Social media report of 1 hail in Canadian. Report relayed by local media.
Copious amounts of half dollar size hail were reported by a storm chaser on U.S. Highway 60 south of Canadian.
A trained spotter and storm chaser reported one inch hail just south of Canadian.

Accumulating hail completely covered State Highway 33, to a depth of 3 to 4 inches, creating a swath which extended east to the Oklahoma state line. Most hail stones were one-half to one inch in diameter with occasional stones of 2 inches noted.
A trained spotter 7 miles south-southwest of Lake Marvin reported quarter size hail.
A storm chaser's reported golf ball size hail 10 miles south of Lake Marvin.
Quarter sized hail was observed 10 miles east-northeast of Lora.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Canadian. This public report was relayed by broadcast media. The time is estimated from radar.
Nickle size hail was reported 1 mile south-southeast of Canadian.
Quarter size hail lasted a few minutes around 2 miles south-southwest of Canadian.
Quarter size hail fell 2 miles northeast of Lora.
Accumulating hail up to an inch or two deep was reported, with the largest size being one inch in diameter.
Light accumulation of hail reported to cover the ground.
Emergency officials reported numerous power poles down and trees uprooted.
Downed power lines have forced the closure | of US HWY 83 at the intersection of | US HWY 60 and US HWY 83.
Law enforcement reported 18 train cars blown over.

Hail of 3 inches in diameter was measured with a ruler and verified via a photo.
Hail fell across Canadian with penny size hail in town and ping pong ball size hail about two miles southeast of Canadian.
Baseball size hail occurred around 12 miles south of Higgins.

The walls of a farm storage building were blown down and the metal roofing blown off. Nearby tree branches were broken off. About three power poles were broken as well.
